sidebar.title: Bots
new.title: New Bot
new.description: A name is all it needs. Say what it’s responsible for now, or tell it later in the chat.
new.name: Name
page.disabledDescription: Bots is a Labs feature. Turn it on in Settings › Labs.
page.emptyDescription: A Bot is a teammate that's always around: one long conversation you can pick up anytime, and chats and schedules can reach it too.
details.instructionsPlaceholder: e.g. You review PRs in the pisper repo; fix small issues directly, otherwise only suggest; run npm test before concluding.
details.acceptsWork: Take messages from chats and schedules
details.permissionHint: It edits files and runs commands on this computer on its own, not only in the starting folder. “Ask only if risky”: it stops to ask only for commands the guard flags as dangerous, clicks and typing in the browser, and third-party plugins. Bots you can call from a group chat can’t use full access.
computer.description: It reads and writes code and runs commands on this computer. You can switch it to another computer running pisper executor.
activity.question: Has a question for you
details.toolsHint: Read only: it can read and search code but not edit files or run commands. Tools outside the scope are blocked before they run.
computer.folderInRoots: Must be inside a folder this computer allows: {roots}
computer.remoteOff: Turn on remote access first so the other computer can reach this one.
computer.runThere: Run this on that computer (replace the folder with the code folder Bots may use; repeat --root for more):
computer.rootHint: That computer only needs Node.js, no model keys.
triggers.chatsHint: In these chats, send “/{name} what to do” or “@Pisper {name} what to do”. Send /whoami in a chat to see its IDs.
triggers.peerIdsPlaceholder: Chat IDs, comma separated; empty means all chats
triggers.senderIdsPlaceholder: Who can call it (IDs, comma separated); empty means only you
triggers.senderIdsRequired: Who can call it (IDs, comma separated); required for groups
triggers.scheduleMessagePlaceholder: e.g. Check dependencies for security updates
triggers.otherSchedule: As set on the Schedules page
new.dutyPlaceholder: e.g. Review PRs in the pisper repo; fix small issues, otherwise only suggest.
new.folderDefault: Leave empty to start in the default working folder
new.folderSummary: Starts in the default working folder on this computer.
settingsPage.title: {name} settings
model.title: Model
model.hint: Its session uses this model and thinking level; changes apply from the next turn. Tiers follow the model tiers in Settings › Subagents.
memory.title: Memory
memory.hint: What {name} remembers: what you asked it to remember, your corrections, and lessons from finished work. Sub-agents it hands work to get these too. It tidies them once a day when idle.
memory.addPlaceholder: e.g. Check the home page on an iPhone before each release
skills.title: What it learned
skills.hint: {name} reviews each finished job: work it will do again gets written down as its own skill, and every sub-agent it hands work to carries its skills. Your corrections update them too.
proactive.title: Proactive
proactive.checkHint: When {name} has nothing to do, it looks over what it is responsible for, read-only (reads and searches files; no edits, no commands, no outgoing messages). Findings become a suggestion in its conversation; it only starts work when you say so.
proactive.briefHint: What was done in the last day, what is scheduled today and any suggestions, written in its conversation.
details.parallelHint: How many sub-agents it runs at the same time; the rest wait in line.
